title: Optimizing Stock Option Forecasting with the Assembly of Machine Learning Models and Improved Trading Strategies

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper applies machine learning models including Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, convolutional neural networks (CNN), and the Quasi-Reversibility Method (QRM) along with the Black-Scholes equation to forecast stock option trends and prices. Models are trained on historical stock and option time-series data. Simulated trading strategies, notably combining machine learning forecasts with a Binomial Asset Pricing Model and stochastic process analysis, are tested to evaluate investment performance.

performance_metrics.context: Classification NN + Model10k CNN combined model precision

key_findings: LSTM and other neural network models can predict stock option pricing and directional trends, though combining interdependent models can lead to lower performance due to shared features and correlation.
A Binomial Asset Pricing Model integrated with machine learning model precision estimates provides a structured framework for calculating expected returns and simulating option portfolios.
Empirical testing indicates that combining existing ML models (such as Classification NN and CNN) yields a lower precision than individual models due to a lack of complete independence.
limitations: The LSTM was trained solely on sequences of fixed length (10 days), making its performance unpredictable on significantly longer sequences.
The independent models shared common features (such as relying on the QRM model's results), creating model dependence and lowering combined forecast precision.
Advanced hedging techniques like the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation were not applied in the binomial trading tree nodes, utilizing a simpler method instead.
